title: Edward Scissorhands
tagline: The story of an uncommonly gentle man.
about: An unfinished man with scissors for hands is taken home by an Avon lady to her pastel suburb, where he trims hedges, cuts hair and falls for her daughter.
cue: Serve the pie when Edward carves the ice and the shavings fall like snow.

    To StartWelcome barbecue chicken skewersThe Boggses throw Edward a barbecue. Sticky barbecue chicken skewers cut into bites.How to make it700g chicken thigh fillets, cut in chunks125ml smoky barbecue sauce1 tbsp honey1 tsp smoked paprika1 tbsp neutral oil8 bamboo skewers, soaked2 spring onions, slicedMix the barbecue sauce, honey, paprika and oil and coat the chicken.Thread onto the skewers.Grill, turning and basting with the sauce, until sticky and cooked through.Scatter with spring onion.Topiary garden green goddess platterEdward trims the hedges into animals. Crisp garden vegetables with herby green goddess dip.How to make it200g Greek yoghurt3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 cup parsley leaves1/2 cup basil leaves2 tbsp chives1 lemon, juiced1 small garlic clove1 bunch baby carrots, trimmed1 Lebanese cucumber, cut in batons200g sugar snap peas1 head broccolini, trimmed250g cherry tomatoesBlitz the yoghurt, mayo, herbs, lemon and garlic until smooth and green, and season.Blanch the broccolini and snap peas for a minute, then cool in iced water.Stand the vegetables up in glasses and bowls like a clipped garden around the dip.Sugar cookies, fresh off the lineEdward began as part of a cookie machine.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsCome home with me glazed meatloafPeg takes Edward home with her. Glazed beef meatloaf with buttery mash and peas.How to make it800g beef mince1 brown onion, grated1 carrot, grated60g fresh breadcrumbs1 egg2 tsp dried thyme125ml tomato sauce, plus 2 tbsp for the mix2 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp apple cider vinegar1kg floury potatoes, peeled60g butter150ml milk300g frozen peasMix the mince, onion, carrot, breadcrumbs, egg, thyme and 2 tbsp tomato sauce with salt and shape into a loaf in a lined tin.Stir the tomato sauce, sugar and vinegar, spread half over the loaf and bake at 180°C.Spread on the rest of the glaze and bake until sticky and cooked through, then rest.Boil and mash the potatoes with the butter and milk, cook the peas, and serve thick slices of loaf on top.Christmas ice sculpture glazed hamEdward carves Kim from ice. Clove-studded maple-glazed ham.How to make it2.5kg half leg ham on the bone125ml maple syrup1 orange, zested and juiced2 tbsp Dijon mustard2 tbsp brown sugar30 whole clovesPeel the rind off the ham, leaving the fat, then score the fat in a diamond pattern and stud with cloves.Simmer the maple, orange, mustard and sugar until syrupy.Bake the ham at 180°C, brushing with glaze every 15 minutes, until deep amber.Rest and carve at the table.Something SweetHarmless as cherry piePeg the Avon lady calls at the castle. Lattice cherry pie with vanilla ice cream.How to make it2 sheets of frozen shortcrust pastry2 x 680g jars of pitted morello cherries, drained, 250ml juice kept100g caster sugar3 tbsp cornflour1 lemon, juiced1 tsp vanilla extract1 egg, beaten1 tbsp raw sugar500ml vanilla ice creamSimmer the cherry juice, sugar and cornflour until thick, then stir in the cherries, lemon and vanilla and cool.Line a pie dish with one pastry sheet, fill with the cherries and cut the other sheet into strips for a lattice.Brush with egg, sprinkle with raw sugar and bake at 200°C until golden and bubbling.Cool a little and serve with ice cream.To DrinkPleased as punch pink lemonadeBill is just as pleased as punch. Pink lemonade punch with berries and mint.How to make it4 lemons, juiced80g caster sugar150g raspberries1 L lemonade, chilled500ml soda water, chilled1 cup mint leaves2 cups iceCrush half the raspberries with the sugar and lemon juice and strain into a punch bowl.Add the ice, lemonade and soda.Float the rest of the raspberries and the mint on top and ladle into glasses.Cold milk for the cookiesYou can't buy the necessities of life with cookies.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
